name: Ajax 1994/95 (Louis van Gaal)
scopeNote: Ajax of the 1994/95 season under Van Gaal: unbeaten Eredivisie, Champions League winners (final 1995-05-24, Milan 1-0, Vienna). Period 1994-08-21 (Supercup) to 1995-05-27 as decided earlier; RSSSF lists the last league match (v Twente, 3-1) on 28 May 1995, see openQuestions. Style named by sources as 3-4-3 with a midfield diamond (Ballverliebt, StatsBomb, La Grinta), 3-1-3-3 / 3-3-1-3 in Ballverliebt and Goal, 3-3-4 in possession (Spielverlagerung, La Grinta after Kluivert came on); the popular label '4-3-3' is called inaccurate by Ballverliebt. Marking: man-to-man by the outer centre-backs (Reiziger, F. de Boer) with Blind as libero (Ballverliebt, La Grinta); midfield also used individual marking vs Bayern. The famous 2-0 wins over Milan are the two group games (1994-09-14 and the return); the Bayern semi-final was 0-0 away and 5-2 home. Some dated events are given as month only because the day was not read in a source. All facts are retrospective (2011-2025), no contemporaneous 1994/95 match report was read. Only the Milan final has a full tactical study (Spielverlagerung, StatsBomb).
openQuestions: Last Eredivisie match: RSSSF lists round 34 v FC Twente (3-1, home) on 28/5/95, not 27 May; the caller's period end 1995-05-27 kept as instructed.

Marking system: two B-tier sources (Ballverliebt, La Grinta) say man-marking by the outer stoppers with Blind as libero; no Dutch-language tactical source was found and no source discusses zonal marking for this Ajax. Set-piece defending marking not found.
Formation label disagrees: 3-4-3 diamond (Ballverliebt, StatsBomb), 3-3-1-3 (Goal.com, citing Van Gaal), 3-1-2-3-1 / 3-5-2 (These Football Times), 4-3-3 or 3-4-3 (FourFourTwo).

Academy count disagrees: FourFourTwo says 13 of the 18 players involved were academy-schooled; StatsBomb says 7 of the 13 players used (6 of the starting XI); Holland Times says 8. The old 13-of-18 figure is therefore not safe.
Average age disagrees: 22 for the starting XI without Blind and Rijkaard, 24 with them (TFT); 23 (FFT); almost 22 (Goal).
Bayern 2-0 wins asked by the caller were not found: the Bayern tie in 1994/95 was 0-0 and 5-2; the 2-0 results are the two group wins over Milan (Ballverliebt).
Pressing: only La Grinta (vs Bayern, Overmars and Kanu pressing the back three, Seedorf on Frey) and Blind's 'we pressured high' give a pressing description; no tier A source on the high line.
Litmanen's role is a #10 who joined the front line (Spielverlagerung), brutal defensive work (Ballverliebt); not independently checked on match footage.

sources.title: When Ajax ruled the world: how Louis van Gaal nurtured his glorious mid-'90s empire (FourFourTwo)
sources.evidence: The whole team moved in set patterns; if one player dropped back to receive the ball, another had to make a run towards the opposition’s goal. The wingers were instructed to repeatedly make forward runs to open up space for a long ball from the back, while midfielders were told to stay behind the wingers at all times. If an attack couldn’t be forged down the one side, they then had to switch the ball to the opposite flank as quickly as possible. All of this was to be played out in the confines of a 4-3-3 or 3-4-3 formation.
